validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: solidly real. This is Iran's principal cross-border gas export trunk to Turkey (the 'Iran-Turkey pipeline'), operating since commissioning in July 2001, with continuous independent reporting of flows, outages and re-starts (Reuters 2007/2008 blast+cold-weather cuts, Shana resumption, Tehran Times 2025 export-surge). Not GEM-derived. CLASSIFICATION: correct — high-pressure gas transmission trunk, international, gas fuel. DUPLICATE CHECK: not a duplicate. The GulfPub PE World Map 'Tabriz - Bazargan Pipeline' (40 in, 157 km, operating) and the second-search figure of a ~265 km 40-in Tabriz->Bazargan Iranian section are just the IRANIAN LEG of this same corridor; GEM models the whole Tabriz->Ankara line (Iran leg + Turkish BOTAS leg via Dogubayazit-Erzurum-Erzincan-Sivas) as one 2,577 km row, which is the standard framing. No other Iran-gas roster PID covers Tabriz->Ankara (P0449 Iran-Armenia also starts at Tabriz but heads north to Armenia — different line). SPEC: length 2,577 km corroborated (Wikipedia, dbpedia; widely repeated); capacity 14 bcm/y design corroborated (Wikipedia) though contracted export volume is 10 bcm/y (pipeline-journal, MEED) and one source cites 20 bcm design — 14 bcm/y is defensible as the design figure; commissioning July 2001 (Wikipedia, MEED 'end of year 2001 start') — GEM StartYear1=2002 is off by ~1 yr (first full-year operation), a minor caveat not worth a concern flag; Iranian-section diameter 40 in confirmed, the paired '46' in for the Turkish trunk is unverified in independent sources (BOTAS trunk usually cited at 48 in) — flagged as a soft caveat, left as-is pending a BOTAS-side confirmation.

validity.researcher_notes: GEM lists Owner1 = 'National Iranian Oil Co' (NIOC). For a gas TRANSMISSION/export line the Iranian counterpart is the National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC), not NIOC (which is the upstream oil company). pipeline-journal states verbatim 'National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC)' as the Iranian party opposite 'BOTAS Petroleum Pipeline Corporation'; Tehran Times and P.A.Turkey report the BOTAS-NIGC export deals. GulfPub tags most Iran lines 'NIOC' generically, which is unreliable for gas. Owner2 = BOTAS is correct. This is a genuine attribution fix, not a spec quibble.

routes.corridor_desc: Runs west from Tabriz (NW Iran) ~265 km on a 40-in line to the Bazargan border, crosses into Türkiye at Doğubayazıt, then follows the BOTAS trunk west across Anatolia via Erzurum, Erzincan and Sivas to Ankara. Total ~2,577 km. Endpoint cities are well-established named termini; waypoint coords are the standard city/border-town locations (defensible, not a surveyed centerline), so the corridor is tightly bounded to that town chain but the exact routing between towns is approximate.

summary: P0459 Tabriz-Ankara: real, correctly classified gas export trunk (operating 2001, 2577 km, 14 bcm/y all corroborated); ONE attribution concern — Iranian owner should be NIGC not NIOC; StartYear 2002 vs 2001 and Turkish-side 46-in diameter are soft caveats; dead GECF ref replaced with verified independent refs.
